decidedBy: the project owner, 2026-10-29, written onto the records by claude-opus-5-5 on 2026-10-29
policy: Sosthenes is not Crispus and Epaphras is not Epaphroditus: the text names them as different men. Where the text does not join the men of one name it holds them apart, a record per group of verses that belong together: Sosthenes the ruler of the synagogue (ACT 18:17) and Sosthenes our brother (1CO 1:1); Gaius the Macedonian (ACT 19:29), Gaius of Corinth (ROM 16:23; 1CO 1:14) and the Gaius of 3 John (3JN 1:1); Erastus whom Paul sent into Macedonia and who stayed at Corinth (ACT 19:22; 2TI 4:20) and Erastus the chamberlain of the city (ROM 16:23). Each says whom some identify him with.
source: Essenthos, on the project owner's decision of 2026-10-29 that the men of Paul's circle the text does not join are held apart

create.name: Sosthenes
create.distinguisher: the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, beaten before Gallio's judgment seat (ACT 18:17)
create.notes: He may also be 'Sosthenes our brother', with whom Paul writes his first letter to the Corinthians (1CO 1:1), as many identify him; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat' (ACT 18:17): Acts names Crispus the chief ruler of the synagogue in 18:8 and Sosthenes in 18:17, two men.

create.name: Sosthenes
create.distinguisher: 'our brother', with whom Paul writes his first letter to the Corinthians (1CO 1:1)
create.notes: He may also be Sosthenes the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, whom the Greeks beat before Gallio's judgment seat (ACT 18:17), as many identify him; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother' (1CO 1:1): Sosthenes, not Crispus, and not joined by the text to the ruler of the synagogue of ACT 18:17.

create.name: Epaphras
create.distinguisher: of Colossae, from whom the Colossians learned the gospel, Paul's fellow prisoner (COL 1:7; 4:12; PHM 1:23)
create.notes: He may also be Epaphroditus, the messenger of the Philippians (PHP 2:25; 4:18), as some identify him, Epaphras being a short form of that name; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant' (COL 1:7): Epaphras of Colossae, whom the text does not call Epaphroditus, the messenger of the Philippians (PHP 2:25).
'Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you' (COL 4:12).
'There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus' (PHM 1:23).

says.notes: He may also be Epaphras of Colossae, Paul's fellow prisoner (COL 1:7; 4:12; PHM 1:23), as some identify him, Epaphras being a short form of his name; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Epaphroditus, my brother, and companion in labour, and fellowsoldier, but your messenger' (PHP 2:25): the messenger of the Philippians, apart from Epaphras of Colossae.

says.notes: He may also be Gaius of Corinth, Paul's host, whom Paul baptized (ROM 16:23; 1CO 1:14), as some identify him; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Having caught Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel' (ACT 19:29): the Macedonian, whom the text does not join to the Gaius of Corinth or of 3 John.

create.name: Gaius
create.distinguisher: Paul's host at Corinth and the host of the whole church, whom Paul baptized (ROM 16:23; 1CO 1:14)
create.notes: He may also be the Macedonian Gaius, Paul's companion in travel (ACT 19:29), or the Gaius to whom the third letter of John is written (3JN 1:1), as some identify him; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Gaius mine host, and of the whole church, saluteth you' (ROM 16:23): Paul's host, whom he baptized at Corinth (1CO 1:14); the text does not make him the Macedonian of ACT 19:29.
'I thank God that I baptized none of you, but Crispus and Gaius' (1CO 1:14): Gaius of Corinth.

says.notes: He may also be Gaius of Corinth, Paul's host, whom Paul baptized (ROM 16:23; 1CO 1:14), as some identify him; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'The elder unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth' (3JN 1:1): the Gaius of 3 John, whom the text does not join to another.

says.notes: He may also be Erastus the chamberlain of the city (ROM 16:23), as some identify him; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'So he sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timotheus and Erastus' (ACT 19:22).
'Erastus abode at Corinth' (2TI 4:20): the Erastus Paul sent ahead with Timothy and who was with him on his journeys, whom the text does not call the chamberlain of the city.

says.notes: He may also be the Erastus whom Paul sent into Macedonia with Timothy and who stayed at Corinth (ACT 19:22; 2TI 4:20), as some identify him; the text does not say.

rulings.why: 'Erastus the chamberlain of the city saluteth you' (ROM 16:23): the city's treasurer, whom the text does not join to the Erastus of ACT 19:22 and 2TI 4:20.
